lark-cli — Lark/Feishu CLI tool.

AGENT QUICKSTART (driving this as an agent? start here):
    Browse commands:  lark-cli <domain> --help            # +shortcuts (preferred) and raw API resources
    Inspect a call:   lark-cli schema <service>.<resource>.<method>   # params, types, scopes, examples
    Prefer a +shortcut over the raw API resource when one matches the task.
    Risk: each command's --help shows read | write | high-risk-write;
          high-risk-write needs --yes, only after the user confirms.
    On any API call: --jq <expr> filters JSON output, --dry-run previews the request (runs nothing).

EXAMPLES (one per command style, in order of preference):
    lark-cli calendar +agenda                                       # +shortcut — a high-level task, prefer these
    lark-cli mail user_mailbox.messages list --user-mailbox-id me   # typed command for one API method
    lark-cli schema mail.user_mailbox.messages.list                 # inspect a method's params before calling
    lark-cli api GET /open-apis/calendar/v4/calendars               # raw escape hatch — any endpoint by HTTP path

Usage:
  lark-cli <command> [subcommand] [method] [flags]
  lark-cli api <method> <path> [--params <json>] [--data <json>]
  lark-cli schema <service.resource.method>

  drive       File, comment, permission, and upload management
  event       Consume and manage real-time events

  mail        Email, draft, folder, and contacts management

  mindnotes   Mindnote node listing, creation, and update

Skills setup (one-time, humans): npx skills add larksuite/cli -g -y — https://github.com/larksuite/cli#agent-skills

Spreadsheet operations

Risk levels (read | write | high-risk-write) appear in each command's --help; high-risk-write requires --yes, only after the user confirms.

Usage:
  lark-cli sheets [flags]

Available Commands:
  +batch-chart-create       Create multiple independent basic charts through one batch request; valid charts continue when another chart fails.
  +batch-chart-update       Update multiple independent chart configurations or data sources through one batch request.
  +batch-update             Execute a batch of write shortcuts in one request; fail-fast on the first failing sub-op (already-applied sub-ops are NOT rolled back).
  +cells-batch-clear        Clear content/formats across many sheet-prefixed ranges in one batch request (irreversible; fail-fast, no rollback).

  +cells-merge              Merge cells in a range.

  +dim-ungroup              Remove a row/column outline group.

  +dropdown-delete          Clear dropdowns from many sheet-prefixed ranges in one batch request (irreversible; fail-fast, no rollback).
  +dropdown-get             Read the dropdown / data-validation configuration on a range.

  +float-image-create       Create a floating image (from a local --image path, or an existing --image-token / --image-uri).
  +float-image-delete       Delete a float-image object (irreversible).
  +float-image-list         List floating images on a sheet, optionally filtered to a single float_image_id.
  +float-image-update       Update an existing floating image (target by --float-image-id; provide the full set of flat flags).
  +formula-verify           Scan formulas / cell errors and return a recalc.py-shaped status report (success / errors_found / partial). Use --ai-only to poll AI-formula compute status only.
  +history-list             List a spreadsheet's edit history versions (history_version_id, create_time, action, all_block_revision).
  +history-revert           Revert a spreadsheet to a given history version (asynchronous; poll with +history-revert-status).
  +history-revert-status    Poll the status of a history revert (in-progress / success / failure).
  +pivot-create             Create a pivot object via the manage_*_object tool.
  +pivot-delete             Delete a pivot object (irreversible).
  +pivot-list               List pivot tables on a sheet, optionally filtered to a single pivot_table_id.
  +pivot-update             Update an existing pivot object (read-modify-write; consult --list first).
  +range-copy               Copy a range to a new location (--paste-type controls what is copied).
  +range-fill               Autofill a target range from a source template (copy / linear / growth / date series).
  +range-move               Cut a range and paste it at a new location (optionally cross-sheet).
  +range-sort               Sort rows within a range by one or more columns.
  +revision-get             Get the spreadsheet's current document revision (version number).
  +rows-resize              Resize rows in pixels: --range + --height <px> for one uniform height, --heights '{"1":50,"2:20":30,"21":"auto"}' for per-row heights in one batch request, or --type standard/auto (--range is 1-based A1 like "2:10" or "5").
  +sheet-copy               Duplicate a sub-sheet, optionally renaming and repositioning the copy.
  +sheet-create             Create a new sub-sheet with an optional position and initial dimensions.
  +sheet-delete             Delete a sub-sheet (irreversible).
  +sheet-hide               Hide a sub-sheet from the tabs bar.
  +sheet-hide-gridline      Hide gridlines on a sub-sheet.
  +sheet-info               Get a sub-sheet's layout metadata: row heights, column widths, hidden rows/cols, merges, groups, freeze.
  +sheet-move               Move a sub-sheet to a new position.
